drug_class: Serotonin modulator antidepressant (SARI - Serotonin Antagonist and Reuptake Inhibitor)
purpose: Nefazodone is used to treat depression, including the feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest that come with it. It can also help improve sleep problems and anxiety that often go along with depression. Your doctor may sometimes prescribe it for other mood-related conditions as well.
how_it_works: This medication works by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain, especially one called serotonin. It both blocks certain serotonin receptors and prevents your brain from reabsorbing serotonin too quickly, which helps keep your mood more stable. Think of it as helping your brain hold onto the 'feel good' messages for a little longer so they can do their job.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, headache, blurred or abnormal vision (sometimes seeing halos or having trouble with low-light vision), constipation, and feeling lightheaded when you stand up quickly.
warnings: IMPORTANT: Nefazodone carries a serious warning about rare but potentially life-threatening liver damage. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, or unusual fatigue. Do not take this medication if you have liver problems. It can also cause a rare but dangerous condition called serotonin syndrome if combined with certain other medicines. Do not take it with MAO inhibitors. It may increase thoughts of suicide in young people, especially when first starting the medication, so close monitoring is essential.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg taken twice a day (morning and evening) with or without food. Your doctor will likely increase your dose gradually, aiming for 300 to 600 mg per day split into two doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, and never stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
